articles.body:
Playing solo for the first time and looking for a small clarification.

The crown is commander and I am considering whether they will purchase a local alliance.  Climate is peacock, so ‘if the crown’s army strength is 2+’ they will attempt to purchase an alliance.

What is the crown’s army strength?  Is this term defined anywhere?
articles.bodyXml:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<xml><safehtml>Playing solo for the first time and looking for a small clarification.<br/><br/>The crown is commander and I am considering whether they will purchase a local alliance.  Climate is peacock, so ‘if the crown’s army strength is 2+’ they will attempt to purchase an alliance.<br/><br/>What is the crown’s army strength?  Is this term defined anywhere?</safehtml></xml>

articles.body: Officers + regiments in that army, same as the normal game.
articles.bodyXml:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<xml><safehtml>Officers + regiments in that army, same as the normal game.</safehtml></xml>

articles.body:
Thanks - I am not sure where Army Strength ever appears as a term in the normal game?

I specifically found it unclear whether it included non-crown officers and regiments.

articles.body:
I don't think "Army Strength" ever appears as a defined term to be honest. [i]JoCo[/i] could certainly do with a clearly and more consistent rulebook (GMT style).

I've always taken "Crown army" to mean an army where the Crown is the Commander. So "[i]if the crown’s army strength is 2+[/i]" means there has to be at least two officers/regiments in that army (the family the officers belong to is irrelevant).

So "<em>if the crown’s army strength is 2+</em>" means there has to be at least two officers/regiments in that army (the family the officers belong to is irrelevant).</safehtml></xml>

articles.body: [q]What is the crown’s army strength? Is this term defined anywhere?[/q] the strength is the number of dice the army would roll when deploying.

articles.body:
[q="felipe1982"][q]What is the crown’s army strength? Is this term defined anywhere?[/q] the strength is the number of dice the army would roll when deploying. [/q]

Thanks, and I do get the idea now, but even that’s not quite true because a (human) player can choose to use however many officers/regiments they like.

So I think it’s the number of dice they ‘could’ roll when deploying.  It’s reasonably intuitive once you know all the rules (but not at all this morning while I was learning them!)
